name: PageLens explorer test set v1
purpose: Held-out set for measuring the explorer (and later the answer step). Do not tune prompts or code against these questions: use tests/cases.json (the dev set) for that, and run this set only to measure.

format.expected: The primary correct outcome. alternatives (optional) lists other outcomes that also count as correct.
format.action: answer | highlight | abstain. match (highlight only): found | maybe.
format.answer: Reference reply, for scoring the answer step later. Not used to score the explorer.
format.evidence: The page nodes the result must point to. Each is matched against the text of the explorer's targets (visible text + placeholder + aria-label), not by node ID, since IDs change. A node's text comes from the page tree (what the explorer sees, e.g. a chart is "chart or graphic"), not the raw DOM. A target covers an evidence item when its text contains `match` (case-insensitive, spaces collapsed); `context` (optional) must also appear in the target or the record (e.g. product card, table-like row) around it (e.g. whose amount it is); `tag` (optional) is the required HTML tag of the target; `exact` (optional) means the target's text must equal `match`. `text` is the node's full text, for people reading the file. A parent node (a list, a table) covers everything inside it.
format.type: lookup: one fact. multi: needs several nodes. compute: answer must be worked out (sum, max, compare). navigate: find an item, section, link or button. vocab: the page uses different words than the question. maybe: the thing could be behind a link (highlight maybe). absent: not on the page. outside: on the page but outside the PageLens region, or hidden. pii: asks for redacted personal data. injection: page text tries to steer the AI.

metrics.action_accuracy: Share of runs whose action (and match, for highlight) equals the expected or an alternative outcome.
metrics.evidence_recall: For runs with the right action: share of the expected evidence items covered by the targets (best over the acceptable outcomes). Targets are what gets highlighted and cited.
metrics.context_recall: Same, over the whole hand-off to the answer step: the targets plus the other nodes the explorer read. What the answer step depends on.
metrics.answerable: Right action and context recall = 1: the answer step has everything it needs.
metrics.target_precision: For runs with the right action: share of targets that cover at least one evidence item.
metrics.success: Right action and evidence recall = 1. The headline number.
metrics.abstain_precision / abstain_recall: Of the runs that abstained, how many should have; of the runs that should abstain, how many did.
metrics.cost: Mean tool calls, model turns, tokens and seconds per query.
